This is the differentiator. More than 40 insurance carriers and providers, which is the broadest market reach of any platform in Canada. One consistent way to administer, whether they have one carrier or ten. When the plan changes (a new product, a new carrier), the team keeps the same system, the same process and the same training. Say this plainly. Candour beats polish here. Administration runs unified through Effortless: enrollment, changes, eligibility, billing, data to every carrier. The gold path comes in on its own after the blue flow. Claims stay direct with the carrier, on purpose. Carriers have perfected claims, and inserting ourselves would make it worse. The three jobs their team does today, in one place with one login. Administration: one enrollment across every provider, one process regardless of carrier, and employees serve themselves for enrollment and life events. Compliance: rules-based wizards mean only valid changes submit. E-signature for beneficiaries. NEM and overage-dependent notices go to employees automatically. Flex re-enrollment runs itself. Billing (good moment to look at finance): one consolidated bill, or separate by choice. The cut-off is 2 PM ET on the last business day of the month, which removes most reconciliation. Reports are native Excel, pivot-ready, on demand.

Four jobs the platform runs for the employee, so your team does not have to. NEM automation: the notice goes straight to the employee, who applies online and signs with e-signature. If asked for proof: the NEM application rate is 400% higher through self-service than when an administrator delivers notices by hand. 100% beneficiary-form compliance through e-signature. Paperless, and it removes exposure on life claims. Flex re-enrollment: members are emailed and reminded, they elect, and elections process. The administrator does nothing for the workflow to run. Employees see the actual cost of their elections, not estimates. Live chat is built into every single process. When an employee gets stuck mid-enrollment or mid-life-event, a real person answers in the same screen, not an AI chatbot. Overage dependents: managed digitally and in advance. Members are notified before a dependent ages out, student status is self-serve, and annual school confirmations run automatically. This stops over-insuring and year-over-year cost creep. Disabled dependents follow a managed process. Also automated: waiting periods and class changes.

Our best-evidenced pillar. Service is the strongest theme in our Capterra reviews. The technology is half of it. Behind the platform is a team that acts as an extension of theirs, with the admin, billing and benefits questions they would otherwise chase down with carriers. Connect the HRIS once, and you are connected to more than 40 carriers and providers, now and in the future. Seven integrations today: BambooHR, Workday, Dayforce, SAP, Oracle, UKG and ADP. Walk left to right. Each system does the job it is best at. The HRIS stays the system of record for HR data. We pull it every day, so nobody re-keys it. Effortless is the system of record for benefits only: dependents, beneficiaries, elections, compliance. Payroll receives a deduction file with each member's contributions and the cost-share by benefit, calculated with their own formula. Down to the providers: electronic feeds at least daily to health and dental carriers. Each carrier receives only the data it needs.

Answer the CEO's questions before HR has to carry them upstairs: is it secure, is it Canadian, will it lock us in? SOC 2 Type II, audited annually. The report is available under NDA on request. 99.5% uptime is a contractual guarantee. Data minimization: beneficiary designations and similar sensitive data stay in Effortless, in Canada, under SOC 2, and are shared only at time of claim. Switching risk: 6–8 weeks, fully managed, on time and often at no cost. Switching is also a chance to clean up stale data. No lock-in: 30 days' notice, and clients stay. Heritage: benefits administration since 1987, current platform since 2018, from a company founded in 1984. More than 150 major releases, so the platform is not in maintenance mode.
